bengaluru.character: Bengaluru (Kannada: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು Bengaḷūru), formerly Bangalore, is the largest city in southern India and the capital of the state of Karnataka.

landmarks.name: Gopalan Cinemas
landmarks.note: Gopalan Mall, Mysore Road; Gopalan Mall, Near Jayadeva Hospital, Bannerghatta Road ; Gopalan Mal;, Old Madras Road, Near Baiyappanhalli Metro Station

landmarks.name: Bangalore Film Society
landmarks.note: A club membership (around ₹500/year) is typically required for entrance.

food.note: Restaurants to the south of Bengaluru.
Chain restaurant inspired by Chinese & Thai cuisines, spread across Bengaluru.
Very nice North India cuisine.
Possibly have a few more branches elsewehere in Bengaluru.

food.where: Jayanagar 3rd Block; DVG Road, Gandhi Bazaar
food.note: One of Bengaluru's oldest food joints.

hyderabad.character: right|thumb|The view from the Charminar Hyderabad, (Telugu: హైదరాబాద్ Haidarābād, Urdu: حیدر آباد Haidar Ābād), the "Pearl City", is the capital of the state of Telangana.

landmarks.name: Heritage walk
landmarks.note: They are organized by the Telangana tourism department and led by a knowledgeable guide and Tourist Police.

landmarks.name: Hatsclub Hyderabad Adventure & Trekker’s club
landmarks.note: Active and well-organised trekker’s group organising out of the Hyderabad area.

landmarks.name: Friends of Snakes Society
landmarks.note: For reptile conservation work and field trips.

food.note: Dum refers to the baking process and basmati rice and meat or vegetables are mixed in a pot and heated for a long time.
A dessert made from bread, milk and dry fruits.
A favourite drink of Hyderabad.
Made from a buck/billy/young goat, and is associated with the Hyderabadi cuisine.
A dish that is available only during the month of Ramadaan (Ramzan).

jaipur.character: Jaipur (Hindi: जयपुर Jaypur), also known as the Pink City, is the capital of Indian state of Rajasthan, and its largest city.

landmarks.name: Amber Fort
landmarks.note: This massive fort-palace complex built in hybrid Hindu-Muslim style dates back to Raja Man Singh and was the royal palace of the Kachwahas from c. 1600-1727.

landmarks.name: Jaigarh Fort
landmarks.note: Never conquered in battle, this was considered the strongest of the three forts in the area.

landmarks.name: Nahargarh Fort
landmarks.note: The smallest of the three forts, notable primarily for excellent views over Man Sagar lake and the vast sprawl of Jaipur.

landmarks.name: City Palace
landmarks.note: An imposing blend of traditional Rajput and Mughal architecture.

landmarks.name: Hawa Mahal
landmarks.note: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Singh as part of City Palace, it was an extension of the Zenana (women's) chamber.

landmarks.name: Jal Mahal
landmarks.note: This beautiful Jal Mahal or water palace was made by the King of Amber in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake.

landmarks.name: Birla Mandir (aka The Marble Temple)
landmarks.note: This is a relatively new temple made of white marble with beautiful carvings.

landmarks.name: Galtaji
landmarks.note: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage site.

food.note: Sweets for chamcham, also baked sweets and crispy samosas.
A popular ice-cream parlor on MI Rd. An assortment of ice cream shakes, and some indigenous ice cream flavours.
The gourmet bakery and Italian restaurant is operated by chefs of Hotel Clarks Amer and serves exquisite bakery items, it also serves vegan and veget…

food.where: 2nd Floor, KK Square, C-11 Prithviraj Road
food.note: Mostly organic non-Indian-style ("international flavour") home-style cakes, freshly prepared sandwiches, pastries, savoury snacks plus organic coffee…

food.where: In the Hotel Ramsingh Palace, B 2, Hathi Babau Ka Bagh, Kanti Nagar, Banipark
food.note: Serving vegetarian and vegan, Chinese food and barbecue atop a 100-foot-high building providing a breathtaking view of the city.

mumbai.character: Mumbai (Marathi and Hindi: मुंबई Mumbaī), formerly known as Bombay, is the largest city in western India and the capital of the state of Maharashtra.

landmarks.name: Join for heritage walks
landmarks.note: organised by two architects, these walks take you around various historic and architecturally significant areas of the city.

landmarks.name: Banganga Festival
landmarks.note: (Jan) The musical festival is organised by Maharashtra Tourism (MTDC) annually at Banganga Tank on Malabar Hill.

landmarks.name: Elephanta Festival
landmarks.note: (March) Organised by Maharashtra Tourism, the festival of music and dance at Elephanta Caves has in the past seen performances by renowned artists like Alarmel Valli, Sa…

landmarks.name: Kala Ghoda Festival
landmarks.note: The arts and crafts festival is held in the last week of Jan or first week of Feb annually in the historic precinct of Kala ghoda in Mumbai.

shimla.character: Shimla (Hindi: शिमला), previously spelt Simla, is the capital of the state of Himachal Pradesh in India.

landmarks.name: Christ Church
landmarks.note: Constructed in 1846, this is the second oldest church in North India.

landmarks.name: The Ridge
landmarks.note: The Ridge is the center of Shimla's cultural and social life - an excellent place to view the surrounding mountains.

landmarks.name: Jakhoo Temple
landmarks.note: A temple and the world's largest Hanuman statue.

landmarks.name: Tara Devi Temple
landmarks.note: Tara Devi is famous for its 250-year-old temple.

landmarks.name: Sankat Mochan Temple
landmarks.note: A popular Hanuman temple which can be reached by car or on foot.

landmarks.name: Chadwick Falls
landmarks.note: The waterfall is at its most beautiful just after the monsoon.

landmarks.name: Hip Hip Hurray Amusement Park
landmarks.note: An amusement offering adventure activities like Burma bridge crossing, Flying Fox, rock climbing, boating, various rides, indoor golf & video games.

landmarks.name: Lower Bazaar
landmarks.note: Shops open M-Sa. The Lower Bazaar is home to the city's less expensive hotels, cheaper restaurants and shops, and a congested wholesale vegetable market.

food.where: The Band Stand, The Ridge, Lower Bazaar
food.note: Whatever little can be had of Himachali cuisine can be found at these twin-restaurants run by Himachal Tourism, the one located above the other.
Serves good Indian food of every description complemented by some Chinese and Continental dishes; one of the very few restaurants in town with food a…
Possibly the cheapest food in Shimla, especially during peak season.
Below rain shelter, restaurant with view.
A good selection of European and Asian dishes.

varanasi.character: Varanasi (वाराणसी Vārāṇasī), also known as Banaras (बनारस Banāras) or Kashi (काशी Kāshī), is a holy city at the banks of the Ganges River in Uttar Pradesh, India.

landmarks.name: Jantar Mantar
landmarks.note: Jantar Mantar literally means a combination of instruments and formulas (jantar = instrument and mantar = formula).

landmarks.name: Manikarnika Ghat
landmarks.note: The main cremation ghat; a must-see, but remain quiet and avoid taking photographs (scams are plentiful here; see the "Stay Safe" section).

landmarks.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
landmarks.note: Known as the 'main' ghat, this is the site of the large evening aarti ceremony.

landmarks.name: Shivala Ghat
landmarks.note: The ghat was constructed by King Balwant Singh and played an important role during the Middle Ages.

landmarks.name: Assi Ghat
landmarks.note: A popular place for tourists, long-term students and researchers to stay, with many hotels, restaurants, and internet cafes nearby.

landmarks.name: Lal Khan Tomb
landmarks.note: Lal Khan was the minister and commander of Balwant Singh (reign: 1740 – 70) the King of Varanasi (then Banaras).

landmarks.name: Gyanvapi Mosque
landmarks.note: A rather controversial mosque built during the rule of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.

landmarks.name: Durga Mandir
landmarks.note: Built in the 18th century, the Durga temple was made as a tribute to Goddess Durga.

food.note: One of the myriad guest house rooftop restaurants in Varanasi and not a particularly memorable one at that.
Great food cooked only by mum and family.
One of a number of restaurants along Bangali Tola, this place is great for breakfast as they have a full on espresso machine and serve good food.
A good bakery run by a German baker in Varanasi.
The food and service are good, not great, but the real reason to come here is for the rooftop overlooking the Ghats and the river.

dehradun.character: Dehradun (Hindi: देहरादून Dehrādūn) is the winter capital of the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

landmarks.name: The Kalinga War Memorial
landmarks.note: The only war memorial of its kind in the world which was erected by the British to honour their foe, the Gurkhas (or the Gorkhas).

landmarks.name: The Forest Research Institute Museums
landmarks.note: Lavish environs and one of the largest institutes of its kind.

landmarks.name: Robber's Cave
landmarks.note: Robber's cave is a beautiful picnic spot.

landmarks.name: Chetwoode Hall
landmarks.note: The Indian Military Academy.

landmarks.name: Clock Tower
landmarks.note: Built by the British, this remains the icon of the downtown area.

landmarks.name: Kalsi
landmarks.note: Small town in the Dehradun District with ancient monuments such as the Edicts_of_Ashoka.

landmarks.name: RIMC
landmarks.note: RIMC is one of the finest schools in India for training young men to become a part of the Indian Armed Forces.

landmarks.name: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology
landmarks.note: Another place worth a visit is the Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology.

food.note: One of the finest bar and multicuisine restaurant in Dehradun in a soothing ambience.
Delicious food and amazing ambiance with live ghazals.
This well-known multicuisine restaurant serves Chinese, Indian and Continental food.
One of the best restaurants for authentic Tibetan fare located on Rajpur Road close to the Old Mussoorie Road diversion.
Famous for North Indian fast food.

dharamsala.character: thumb|350px|McLeod Ganj and the snow-capped peaks of the Dhauladhars Dharamsala or Dharamshala (Hindi: धर्मशाला Dharmshālā; Tibetan: དྷ་རམ་ས་ལ་), is a hill station in Himachal Pradesh, famed for its large Tibetan commun…

landmarks.name: HPCA Cricket Stadium
landmarks.note: The picturesque Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association Stadium is unique in India as it is situated at an altitude of 1,457 m above the sea level and has the snow-capped H…

landmarks.name: Dal Lake
landmarks.note: Fairly well signposted. An anticlimactic sacred pond is the colour and texture of its yellow lentil namesake.

landmarks.name: Tibet Museum
landmarks.note: Small but interesting museum on the history of Tibet and its people.

landmarks.name: Bhagsu Temple Swimming Pool
landmarks.note: Go swimming in Bhagsu's very own swimming pool.

landmarks.name: Lha Charitable Trust
landmarks.note: Learn to make different kinds of momos, Tibetan breads and Tibetan noodles.

landmarks.name: Kunal Pathari
landmarks.note: People come to this temple every day to pray to the Goddess.

landmarks.name: Naddi View Point
landmarks.note: This is an ideal place for a complete scenic view of snow covered Dhauladhar range.

landmarks.name: Rakkar
landmarks.note: A picturesque hamlet on the outskirts of Lower Dharamsala, perched on the foothills of the snow capped Dhauladhar range of the Himalayas in the Indian state of Himachal…

food.note: A non-profit café set up as a meeting place between Chinese and Tibetans that holds many discussions and shows promoting harmony and understanding be…
A cozy little hole-in-the-wall place with 5 tables, a counter and a dog.
A bare-bones somewhat dingy but gourmet café prized for its momos.
Decent Western fare of lesser quality with some Tibetan dishes.
A down-to-earth (in every sense) and somewhat drab breakfast place, offering egg dishes (₹20–45), porridge (with mixed fruit, ₹65), toast, sandwiches…

haridwar.character: Haridwar (Hindi: हरिद्वार Haridvār), also spelt Hardwar, is a Hindu pilgrimage site at the Ganges River, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

landmarks.name: Chandi Devi Temple
landmarks.note: A temple dedicated to Chandi Devi on the Neel Parvat.

landmarks.name: Har Ki Pauri
landmarks.note: To the north of the centre, this is Haridwar's focal point, where devotees gather to bathe and worship on the Ganges.

landmarks.name: Maya Devi Temple
landmarks.note: Located on upper road. This temple is one of the 51 Shakti Pithas and it's the presiding deity of Haridwar.

landmarks.name: Mansa Devi Temple
landmarks.note: At top of hill near the centre of town.

landmarks.name: Daksheswar Mahadev Temple
landmarks.note: Daksheswar Mahadev or Daksha Mahadev temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in the Kankhal.

landmarks.name: Rajaji National Park
landmarks.note: While walking around the park you can spot elephants, leopards and deer.

landmarks.name: Bharat Mata Mandir
landmarks.note: Dedicated to Mother India, it is half temple, half nation-building exercise, with seven floors stacked with deities, saints, and secular heroes of all Indian faiths.

landmarks.name: Sureshwari Devi Temple
landmarks.note: Located outside of Haridwar and within the Rajaji National Park, this serene and religious site is a place to see.

food.note: Good for breakfast and lunch.
Claiming to be the original, unfranchised Chotiwalas, this is the first shop right below the steps when walking south from Har Ki Pauri.

food.dish: up a wide menu of South
food.note: The closest Haridwar gets to McDonald's (not very), serves up a wide menu of South and North Indian favourites, with some Indian-Chinese thrown in. M…
This is a tasty Bengali eatery, serving lunch and dinner.
Didir Hotel is a convenient location located at Vishnughat and famous for its multiple serving Thalis.

jammu.character: Jammu (Dogri: जम्मु Jammu), the largest city in the Jammu region of northern India, is the winter capital of Jammu and Kashmir, sitting at a low elevation in the mainly mountainous state.

landmarks.name: Amar Mahal Palace Museum
landmarks.note: A beautiful red sandstone palace that has been converted into a museum.

landmarks.name: Bahu Fort
landmarks.note: 5 km. Situated on a rock face on the left bank of the river Tawi.

landmarks.name: Martand Sun Temple
landmarks.note: The most memorable and beautiful work of King Lalitaditya is the construction of spacious Martand temple, which the emperor got built in honor of the Sun God or Bhaskar.

landmarks.name: Raghunath Mandir
landmarks.note: Situated in the heart of the city and surrounded by a group of other temples.

landmarks.name: Mubarak Mandi Palace
landmarks.note: The oldest buildings in this Palace complex date to 1824.

landmarks.name: Bagh-E-Bahu
landmarks.note: 5 km. These extensive gardens, laid around the Bahu Fort provide a pleasant view of the city.

landmarks.name: Maha Maya Temple and City Forest
landmarks.note: On the By-pass Road behind Bahu Fort, the city forest surrounds the ancient Maha Maya Temple overlooking the river Tawi.

landmarks.name: Peer Kho Cave Temple
landmarks.note: A cave shrine located on the Circular Road, 3.5 km from the heart of the town.

food.note: Huge Utensils to store food and next to bus stand makes it ideal for travellers going in and out of Jammu.
Quite expensive but a favourite among tourists to get their grilled food fix.

leh.character: thumb|Leh Leh (གླེ gle or སླེ sle), the main capital of Ladakh, India, is on the Indus River Valley, at a crossroads of the old trading routes from Xinjiang, Tibet and Kashmir.

landmarks.name: Shanti Stupa
landmarks.note: Built by a Japanese Buddhist group.

landmarks.name: Magnetic Hill
landmarks.note: A supposed optical illusion, where it seems cars rolling down the hill but actually go up. It might not be as impressive as hyped.

landmarks.name: Hall Of Fame
landmarks.note: Fascinating place run by the Indian Army showcasing the history, glory and the equipment related to army operations in some of the most hostile terrain in the world.

landmarks.name: Hemis Monastery
landmarks.note: Supposedly, the largest monastery of Ladakh with at least 150 lamas, but it doesn't look that way.

landmarks.name: Palace of the King of Ladakh
landmarks.note: The palace is the most noticeable building in Leh district; built in the 17th century, and now undergoing restoration.

landmarks.name: Phyang Monastery
landmarks.note: It contains numerous sacred shrines inside the monastery, frescoes dating from the royal period.

landmarks.name: Shey Palace and Monastery
landmarks.note: Shey was once the ancient capital of Ladakh and is now just a rural village.

landmarks.name: Stok Monastery
landmarks.note: A pleasant village across the Indus with this monastery well worth visiting.

food.note: Inexpensive mutton chowmein, tupka and momos.
Another mutton place popular with locals serving thali style dishes and chai.
As everywhere in India, the Gurudwara serves mostly rice and dal throughout the day, but often chai is served as well.

food.dish: Dosa Point by Indian Army - Highest Dosa Point
food.note: Besides what the name of the place indicates, this is one of the most delicious and inexpensive dosa places, probably in the whole of India.
This Gurudwara has one of the better Langars in India, delicious curry with Pakora or tofu.

manali.character: Manali is a city of about 11,000 people (2023) in Central Himachal Pradesh.

landmarks.name: Hidimba Temple
landmarks.note: It is an ancient cave temple dedicated to Hidimbi Devi, who was a character in the Indian epic, Mahābhārata.

landmarks.name: Rohtang Pass
landmarks.note: At an altitude of 3979 m (13,050 ft) above sea level, this is another adventure tourist site where it can be cold even on a summer day.

landmarks.name: Beas Kund
landmarks.note: An igloo-shaped temple, on top has a spring which is the origin of River Beas.

landmarks.name: Old Manali
landmarks.note: 3 km northwest of Manali is Old Manali, famous for its orchards and old guesthouses.

landmarks.name: Rahala waterfalls
landmarks.note: About 16 km from Manali at the start of the climb to the Rohtang Pass, are the beautiful Rahalla Falls at an altitude of 2,501 m.

landmarks.name: Solang Valley
landmarks.note: Popularly known as Snow Point, Solang Valley is 13 km northwest of Manali and famous for its 300-m ski lift.

landmarks.name: Vashist Hot Water Springs and Temple
landmarks.note: Around 3 km from Manali, across the Beas river is Vashist, a small village with natural sulphur springs.

landmarks.name: Naggar
landmarks.note: The Castle, Roerich House and Art gallery are places to see.

food.note: Savour a Himachali menu as well as delectable Indian, European, oriental cuisines.
It is a small eatery with good Indian and Western spread close to the bridge on the Beas River.
Serves cookies, sandwiches, etc., with a complimentary movie theatre offering around 100 films alongside Bob Dylan's music.
A small Spanish-style café with 2 small & 2 cottage rooms available for stay.
The 1st music cafe in Old Manali (near the bridge), on the banks of the River Manalsu.

srinagar.character: thumbnail|right|Shikaras in Dal Lake Srinagar (Kashmiri: سرینگر Sirīnagar, Urdu: سری نگر Srī Nagar) in the Kashmir Valley is the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir and the largest city in the Kashmir region.

landmarks.name: Dal Lake
landmarks.note: Dal Lake is one of the prime attractions of Srinagar.

landmarks.name: Nagin Lake
landmarks.note: Unlike the other three parts of Dal Lake the Nagin Lake is a separate lake connected to the Dal Lake by a narrow water channel.

landmarks.name: Rupa Lank
landmarks.note: Rupa Lank, literally meaning silver island, is in the Dod Dal (central area of Dal Lake).

landmarks.name: Sona Lank
landmarks.note: Sona Lank, literally meaning gold island, is located in Lokut Dal, in the northern part of Dal Lake.

landmarks.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Botanical Garden
landmarks.note: A well-maintained park with lake by Dept of Floriculture with organised parking lot next to the park.

landmarks.name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden
landmarks.note: Located on the eastern side of the Dal Lake, the Tulip Garden covers an area of 30 ha (74 acres) and is the largest tulip garden of Asia.

landmarks.name: Chashme Shahi Garden
landmarks.note: Chashme Shahi is the smallest of the three Mughal gardens of Srinagar, but in spite of its small size, the garden has its share of elegance.

landmarks.name: Nishat Bagh
landmarks.note: Located on the eastern banks of Dal Lake, with the Zabarwan Mountains as its backdrop, the garden was designed in 1633 by Asaf Khan, brother of Nur Jehan.

amritsar.character: Amritsar (Punjabi: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ Aṃmritsar) is a city in the state of Punjab, India.

landmarks.name: Gobindgarh Fort
landmarks.note: A large 1760 fort that is being turned into a tourist spot with several museums and performances.

landmarks.name: Jallianwala Bagh
landmarks.note: The site of the 1919 Amritsar massacre, turned into a park memorial.

landmarks.name: Ram Bagh
landmarks.note: This is a beautiful garden.

landmarks.name: Summer Palace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh'
landmarks.note: The palace houses a museum, exhibiting oil paintings, miniatures, coins and weapons from the Sikh period.

landmarks.name: Baba Atal Rai Tower
landmarks.note: This is a great viewpoint over the city and the nearby Golden Temple.

landmarks.name: Mata Temple
landmarks.note: Highly recommended! This is a cave labyrinth Hindu temple devoted to the female saint Lal Devi.

landmarks.name: Durgiana Temple
landmarks.note: The temple is enshrined with Goddess Durga.

landmarks.name: Golden Temple Complex
landmarks.note: This is the main attraction in the city, and the most important religious place to the Sikhs.

food.note: A dining hall (langar) serving free basic meals to all.

food.where: The Brothers or Bharavan the Dhaba
food.note: Serves traditional food or Chinese, continental at affordable prices.
serves authentic Punjabi food at a very reasonable cost.
Established in 1958. Very popular family restaurant, particularly for butter chicken with naan.
It offers good Punjabi food made in pure ghee.

chandigarh.character: thumb|right|250px|Location of Chandigarh Chandigarh is India's first planned city, quite distinct from the rest of the country and considerably better organised.

landmarks.name: The Capitol Complex
landmarks.note: Most of the capitol complex is fenced off due to tight security, the open hand is accessible and from there you can see the main buildings, albeit from a distance.

landmarks.name: Elante Mall
landmarks.note: Elante Mall at Chandigarh is among the largest malls in North India, covering 20 acres.

landmarks.name: The High Court
landmarks.note: The letter is fine for looking around the High Court; just show it to security at the entrance, around the back, but if you want to take photos you need to surrender you…

landmarks.name: The Legislative Assembly
landmarks.note: This is the Assembly for both Punjab and Haryana.

landmarks.name: Museum and Art Gallery
landmarks.note: The museum and the combined art gallery is an interesting place to go to. Artefacts range from Harappan period relics to paintings and coins from different areas and tim…

landmarks.name: Pinjore Gardens
landmarks.note: Also called Yadavindra Gardens, these are 20 km (12 mi) from Chandigarh and 15 km (9 mi) from Panchkula, on the Chandigarh-Shimla road.

landmarks.name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
landmarks.note: In 1992, Nek Chand, a humble transport official, began to clear a little patch of jungle to make himself a small garden area.

landmarks.name: Rose Garden
landmarks.note: The city houses the largest rose garden in Asia.

food.note: Don't miss this roadside outlet in sector 8.
Online tiffin and food delivery service in Chandigarh at very reasonable price.
buffet grill barbeque restaurant near you.
There is a whole chain of Chawlas, the better ones being in Sector 8 and Sector 22.
Very popular salad bar. Other locations Sector 35, Mohali, Panchkula.

jhansi.character: [http://Jhansi.nic.in Jhansi] is a city in the Northern Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh, India.

landmarks.name: Fort of Jhansi
landmarks.note: The fort of Jhansi was built in 1613, by Raja Bir Singh Judao (1606-27) of Orchha.

landmarks.name: Rani Mahal
landmarks.note: Rani Mahal was built by Raghunath II of Newalkar family (1769-96).

landmarks.name: Barua sagar
landmarks.note: Baruasagar is around 24 km from Jhansi.

landmarks.name: Chirgaon
landmarks.note: Chirgaon is 30 km from Jhansi, It is on the banks of Betwa river.

landmarks.name: St Jude's Shrine
landmarks.note: This shrine of great imortance among Catholic Christians.

landmarks.name: Government Museum
landmarks.note: The Government Museum is in a very picturesque location in the heart of the city.

landmarks.name: Nag Mandir
landmarks.note: This temple is in Jhansi cantonment.

lucknow.character: Lucknow (Hindi: लखनऊ Lakhnaū, Urdu: لکھنؤ Lakhnaū) is the capital of Uttar Pradesh and one of the most populous cities in northern India.

landmarks.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
landmarks.note: A massive church and school.

landmarks.name: Colvin Taluqdars' College
landmarks.note: A must see place with great architecture.

landmarks.name: Kukrail Reserve Forest
landmarks.note: One of the three crocodilian breeding centres in India, including the freshwater gharials (Gavialis gangeticus), one of the 3 native species of crocodilians in India.

landmarks.name: Dilkusha Kothi
landmarks.note: The remains of an 18th-century house built in the English baroque style.

landmarks.name: Bibiapur Kothi
landmarks.note: A neoclassical building built by Nawab Asaf ud-Daula in the late 18th century.

landmarks.name: Bara Imambara
landmarks.note: A large and impressive tomb complex built in 1783.

landmarks.name: Rumi Darwaza
landmarks.note: An imposing gateway built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784, modelled after a historical gate in Constantinople (present-day Istanbul).

landmarks.name: Chota Imambara
landmarks.note: An imposing mausoleum built by the third Nawab of Awadh in 1837.

food.note: You can find great non-vegetarian food here, specially chicken.
Cheap and delicious non-veg food
Famous for its Galawati Kababs.Mainly caters to meat eaters.
This is in the heart of Old Lucknow.
Very good vegetarian food etc.

patna.character: Patna (Hindi: पटना Patnā, pronounced PUHT-nah), the capital of Bihar, is a bustling city in the Indian Plains with a glorious past.

landmarks.name: Golghar
landmarks.note: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.

landmarks.name: Kumhrar
landmarks.note: Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra.

landmarks.name: Bihar Museum
landmarks.note: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar.

landmarks.name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
landmarks.note: A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi.

landmarks.name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
landmarks.note: Among the largest and best planetariums in Asia, it attracts a large number of both domestic and foreign tourists.

landmarks.name: Patna Museum
landmarks.note: It has more than 50,000 rare art objects, with many related to India in the ancient, middle ages and the British colonial era.

landmarks.name: Shrikrishna Science Centre
landmarks.note: The main science museum in the city with over 50 exhibits on physics and mathematics, with an emphasis towards optical illusions.

landmarks.name: Rajendra Smriti Sangrahalaya
landmarks.note: A museum dedicated to Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India.

aurangabad.character: thumb|A painting at the Ajanta caves Aurangabad (Marathi: औरंगाबाद Auraṅgābād), now known officially as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Marathi: छत्रपती संभाजीनगर Chatrapatī Sambhājīnagar), is a city in the Indian state of M…

landmarks.name: Bibi ka Maqbara
landmarks.note: A replica of the Taj Mahal, the Bibi-ka-Maqbara is the only example of the Mughal architecture of its kind in the Deccan plateau.
